stories.title: Deep-sea mining's hidden toll: Heavy metals from polymetallic nodule sediments trigger acute toxicity in mussels
stories.description: In a new study published in Water & Ecology, a research team led by Yonggang Jia from Ocean University of China assesses the acute toxicity of heavy metals released during deep-sea polymetallic nodule mining, using thick-shell mussels (Mytilus coruscus) as a model organism exposed to nodule-bearing sediments from the Clarion-Clipperton Zone. The results reveal selective metal bioconcentration, tissue-specific oxidative stress responses, progressive gill and digestive gland damage, and distinct gene expression strategies across tissues. The findings provide a mechanistic basis for the ecological risk assessment of deep-sea mining and highlight filter-feeding benthic organisms as key sentinels for monitoring mining-related pollution.

stories.title: A digital intervention targeting multiple dimensions of well-being in existing friendship dyads and groups in a randomized controlled trial
stories.description: Emerging adulthood is associated with increased vulnerability to mental health difficulties, lower well-being, and heightened loneliness, highlighting the need for scalable digital interventions. Positive psychology models, particularly the PERMA model, provide a multidimensional framework for promoting well-being. The present preregistered study examined a six-week, PERMA-based, chatbot-delivered intervention designed to mobilize existing friendship networks through structured interaction in dyads and small groups. In this preregistered cluster randomized controlled trial, pre-existing friendship groups were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention or waitlist control condition. The final analytic sample included 251 participants (intervention: n = 124; waitlist control: n = 127). Outcomes included PERMA well-being and its dimensions, perceived social support from friends, loneliness, and interpersonal closeness. Participants in the intervention condition reported higher post-intervention perceived social support from friends and higher scores on the relationships and accomplishment dimensions of PERMA. Within the intervention group, interpersonal closeness also increased across the intervention period. No significant intervention effects were observed for overall well-being, loneliness, positive emotion, engagement, or meaning. These findings suggest that the effects of the intervention were relatively specific rather than broad, with the clearest pattern emerging for participants’ relational experiences. More generally, the study highlights the potential value of considering not only intervention content but also the social context in which digital positive psychology activities are delivered.
